::: {.letter-metadata}
**Date:** Oct 8th [1868]  
**From:** Elderfield, Otterbourne, Winchester.  
**Manuscript:** MS Westcountry Studies Library, Exeter/ Yonge 1868/1[^1]
:::

My dear [Miss Smith](people/person_263.qmd),
Thank you for your kind, warm hearted letter. I know you too know what a great grief is, and how close one clings to the last surviving parent,[^2] and the sense of being still a child at home. May you long preserve that blessing.

I should be very lonely but that my [brother](people/person_1624.qmd) and his [wife](people/person_1604.qmd) are only a garden’s length from me, and most kind, and just at present I have a [cousin](people/person_1582.qmd) with me, who has always been like a sister to me. I think I shall go into Devonshire with her, and then return to face the solitude

yours sincerely
C M Yonge

---

[^1]: Black-edged paper.
[^2]: CMY is replying to a letter of condolence on the death of [FMY](people/person_1606.qmd), who died on 28 September 1868. Ann Carter Smith’s father, the Rev. Richard Carter Smith, perpetual curate of St. Paul’s Charlton, had died on on 1 October 1864.
